content:
❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: The statement is not properly formatted.
Please switch the contribution back to WIP to allow sufficient time for a proper review by others.
Thank you for the feedback! I’ll switch the contribution back to WIP and improve the statement formatting. I’ll review the structure and presentation carefully before requesting another review.

Thanks.

Please follow the example on this page for the formatting and presentation: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement

I'll provide a more detailed review within the next few days. Please keep the contribution in WIP for the time being.

Title
* The archive doesn't feel "fractured".

Goal
* Please remove "THE FRACTURED ARCHIVE".

* Please remove "You must answer connectivity queries as doors are opened and closed."

* The statement is inconsistent in its terminology:

  • It uses both "chambers" and "rooms".

  • It alternates between "opening" and "closing" doors, and "adding" and "deleting" doors.

  For consistency, please make the following changes:

  • Use either "chamber(s)" or "room(s)" throughout this section and the Input and Output sections.

  • Change "currently open" to "currently present".

* Please change "will be given" to "must process".

* "-": Please change "deletes" to "removes".

* "?": Please add "using the doors currently present" after "connected".

Input
* Please change "first line" to "Line 1".

* Please change "next Q lines" to "Next [[Q]] lines" (two changes are needed).

* Please insert "space-separated" between "two" and "integers".

* Please add: "All values in each operation are space-separated".

* Please format the operations. For example, the first operation is formatted like this: {{+}} [[id]] [[u]] [[v]].

Output
* Please format "?" as a {{constant}} and remove the quotation marks.

* Please change "print" to "output".

* Please change "Print" to "Output".

Constraints
* Please format all the [[variables]].

* Please change 5,000 to 1,000 as [[N]] never exceeds 1,000.

* Please change 1,000,000,000 to 1,000 as [[id]] never exceeds 1,000.

* Please change "open" to "present".

* Please change "identifier" to "[[id]]".

* Please move the constraint on [[id]] before the constraint on [[u]] and [[v]], so that the constraints follow the order of the variables in the Input section.

* Please add the following constraints:
[[u]] may be equal to [[v]] in an operation of {{+}} or {{?}}.
Two rooms/chambers (use whichever term you chose earlier) may be connected by multiple doors.

Stub generator
* Please change 100 to 20.

* Please add a write statement, e.g. write YES/NO.

Difficulty
* Please change the difficulty to Medium. This puzzle doesn't warrant a Very Hard rating based on the current test cases.

Cover picture
* Please upload a cover picture for the puzzle.

Cases
* Please remove the trailing newlines from the output for:
  • Validator 3
  • Validator 6
  • Validator 8
  • Validator 10
  • Validator 11
  • Validator 12
  • Validator 13
  • Validator 16
  • Validator 19
  • Validator 22

* I need a little more time to review the cases. I'll get back to you on this point later.

Thanks.

I've reviewed the tests and validators. Below are my observations and suggestions for improving coverage.

* In Pairs 18 to 25, N > 200 and each case contains exactly 140 "?" operations. Across the 16 cases (for the eight pairs), only five have expected YES answers, and none has more than five. In particular, Pairs 20 and 23 end with more than 250 active doors.

Suggestion: Please review the component sizes (where a component is a group of mutually connected rooms) and the query selection in Pairs 18 to 25. A high number of active doors doesn't necessarily imply high connectivity, since doors may be concentrated within a few components. However, if the cases contain large connected components but few queries targeting connected room pairs, consider adjusting the query distribution to improve coverage of YES answers and connectivity changes caused by updates.

* Two rooms can be connected by multiple doors. My initial solution incorrectly treated a "-" operation as removing the connection between two rooms even when another door still connected them. This caused failures in Test 5 and Test 20. I then added a check for whether another door existed between (u, v), which resolved all failures except Test 20. Checking both (u, v) and (v, u) was necessary to pass all the cases, because the input may represent the same undirected connection in either endpoint order.

Suggestion: Please add targeted scenarios in Validators 5 and 20 that cover parallel doors added in both endpoint orders. In particular, after removing one of two parallel doors, the rooms should remain connected; after removing the last door between them, they should become disconnected unless an alternative path exists.

* There are very few instances (only 19 out of 4,306 "?" operations across all cases) that query pairs of rooms with a direct door between them.

Suggestion: Consider adding more direct-edge queries across the test cases, while retaining sufficient coverage of indirect paths and disconnected pairs. This would help verify that solutions correctly handle different types of connectivity, rather than relying on a narrow distribution of query scenarios.
